description: End states every sync engine must reach. The device and the cloud start in agreement on the notes in `synced` (a case may give its own). The device then changes things offline (`local`) while another device changes the cloud (`elsewhere`), and the device syncs. `expected` lists the notes on the device and in the cloud afterwards, sorted, each written as `title: content`, then ` #label` for each label in name order, then ` [x] text` or ` [ ] text` for each checklist item in position order. Engines that can download and upload separately (web, Rust) run every case in each of `orders` and must reach the same end state both ways: AUD-I01 was exactly an outcome that depended on the order. Kotlin syncs in one call and runs each case once. Nothing may be lost: a conflict ends with both versions somewhere.
changes: A change is null (nothing), the string "delete" (delete note 1), an object, or a list of objects. An object acts on note `note` (1-based index into synced, default 1) and may carry `delete: true`, `edit` (new content), `labels` (the note's new label names), `check` (the text of a checklist item to tick), or `create` ({title, content}: a new note, ignoring `note`).
